_comment: Hand-written plugins.json for checks.dev-plugins: basic-config's lock plus a non-empty
localPlugins, which no other fixture has.
make-env reads only the *keys* of localPlugins; every one of them routes to <devPath>/<name>,
and the value is never looked at. The two entries pin that from both sides:
dirred.nvim has a `dir`, deliberately pointing somewhere devPath would never produce, so the
check fails loudly if anyone starts reading it. It is ignored not because it is machine-
specific -- a dir the user wrote absolute is recorded verbatim -- but because a spec-level
dir short-circuits lazy before dev.path is ever consulted (lua/lazy/core/meta.lua:214-217),
so reading it could not change any resolved directory. See the plan's SS3.3 and SS7 R1.
bare.nvim has no `dir` at all, so make-env must not need one. This shape used to be hand-made
only: extract.lua dumped `dir = p.dev and p.dir or nil`, and lua/lazy/core/meta.lua:229-238
always filled a dev plugin's dir in (measured: a bare `dev = true` came out
{"dev":true,"dir":"<HOME>/projects/..."}), so no lock could ever emit a dev entry missing
`dir`. #47's local_dir can return nil for a `dev = true` plugin whose own dev.path happens to
point back under lazy's own root -- a pathological config, see the plan's SS7 -- and
resolve.lua's `p.dev or p.dir` then falls back to `dev` alone, so a real lock can now write
exactly this shape too. It stands for that case, and for a plugins.json written by an older
or future resolve.lua that omits the key outright, and it is what makes `v.dir` reintroduced
without an `or` fallback fail here rather than in a user's config.
What a real lock *does* produce is a dir-bearing entry like dirred.nvim -- either the path lazy
derived from dev.path, or the one the spec wrote (verbatim if absolute, norm'd if it began
with ~). Only this fixture's literal `~` is unrealistic; it is kept because it contrasts so
visibly with devPath. A plugin that sets `dir` without `dev` at all now produces exactly that
shape too (#47).
